_comment: MCP server config loaded by the `claude` CLI in agent/Dockerfile's image (see docker-compose.yml `agent` service, --mcp-config). Plain JSON has no comment syntax, so notes live in these _comment keys instead — the `claude` CLI ignores unknown keys, and the sibling Jobs project's docker/mcp.json (heavily-commented everywhere else) is itself comment-free, evidence the same convention already held there. ${VAR:-default} below is Claude Code's documented env-var expansion for .mcp.json; it reads this container's actual environment (docker-compose.yml `agent` service), so it stays correct if either default ever changes there.

truthcv._comment: TruthCV's own tool surface: generate_cover_letter, record_application, record_screening, check_cooldown, get_canonical_cv, get_profile_answers, record_company_board, get_job_profiles, recommend_salary (mcp/server.py, APIRouter(prefix='/mcp')). The default is the in-network address of the `app` compose service — reachable only from inside the compose network, not from the host or the open internet.

interceptor._comment: PRIMARY browser driver. The `claude` CLI spawns `interceptor mcp serve` over stdio in-container (a process tree under the docker-compose agent service). That subprocess shells to the real `interceptor <verb>` command, which dials the bind-mounted unix socket at INTERCEPTOR_SOCKET_PATH to reach the HOST interceptor daemon, which in turn reaches Chrome via native messaging. Host Chrome is the only path to the operator's logged-in sessions (ATS, SSO, etc.) on which unattended applying depends; see agent/Dockerfile's BROWSER STRATEGY comment for the full reasoning.

_fallbackComment: Playwright (an in-container browser, as the retired Jobs project's docker/mcp.json used) remains the documented FALLBACK per architecture, not configured as a live server above: agent/Dockerfile deliberately installs no browser at all, so a `playwright` entry here could not actually launch anything. Host Chrome via `interceptor mcp serve` (connected to the bind-mounted unix socket reaching the host daemon) is the primary and intended path because it alone preserves the operator's logged-in ATS/SSO sessions, which a fresh containerised browser cannot reproduce. Re-adding `playwright` here would require re-adding a browser to agent/Dockerfile, undoing that decision — see agent/RUNBOOK.md's note that browser tooling is whatever the environment provides.
